entries.name: 300 mm CMOS foundry processing for quantum devices
suppliers: Tier-1 foundry ecosystem (unnamed in sources); Quantum Motion's customized 300 mm line
entries.note: The decisive capability for the silicon-spin thesis: quantum-dot devices that survive full industrial design rules.

entries.name: High-volume silicon-photonics foundry manufacture
entries.note: Photonic approaches' structural claim: the same industrial base that built telecom optics can build quantum components.

entries.name: Dilution refrigeration (sub-100 mK, scaled)
suppliers: Bluefors / Oxford Instruments class suppliers (generic; not source-bound in Genesis)
entries.note: Cross-architecture dependency: nearly every utility-scale design bottoms out in cooling capacity and wiring volume at mK temperatures. Whoever supplies large dilution capacity at acceptable cost sits under most plausible futures.

entries.name: Cryo-CMOS control electronics
suppliers: Quantum Motion (validated cryogenic ICs, per company account)
entries.note: Co-integrated control at deep-cryogenic temperatures is the silicon-spin answer to the wiring wall.

entries.name: Isotopically enriched silicon (²⁸Si)
suppliers: Specialty isotope-supply chain (not source-bound in Genesis)
entries.note: ²⁸Si removes nuclear-spin decoherence; enrichment capacity is a shared upstream dependency.

entries.name: Single-photon sources at component scale
entries.note: Fabrication-tolerant, high-quality sources are the photonic feedstock.

entries.name: Photon-number-resolving / superconducting single-photon detectors
suppliers: PsiQuantum (superconducting thin-film detectors in the fab process)
entries.note: Detection efficiency and dark count set the loss budget directly.

entries.name: Barium-titanate fast optical switching
suppliers: PsiQuantum (BTO developed and produced in-house, San Jose)
entries.note: Low-loss, high-speed switching is where photonic routing becomes manufacturable or not.

entries.name: Low-loss silicon-nitride waveguides
entries.note: Waveguide loss is the quiet budget line in every photonic architecture.

entries.name: Low-loss chip-to-fibre coupling
entries.note: Chip-to-chip interconnect demonstrated at 99.72% conditional fidelity; unconditional performance is part of the loss-budget question.

entries.name: Precision ion traps and zone control
entries.note: Trap fabrication and shuttling control bound trapped-ion scaling.

entries.name: Stable laser systems (trapping and gates)
entries.note: Laser stability and count scale with trap/zone complexity — a shared optical-infrastructure dependency.

entries.name: UHV vacuum packaging
entries.note: Utility-scale atomic systems need industrial-quality vacuum enclosures, not lab rigs.

entries.name: Superconducting-circuit fabrication
entries.note: Mature relative to alternatives; uniformity and materials losses still bind fidelity.

entries.name: Room-temperature control electronics
entries.note: Channel count and synchronization scale with qubit count.

entries.name: Cryogenic wiring and interconnect density
entries.note: The wiring wall: signal lines into mK space grow faster than qubits unless control moves down-temperature.

entries.name: Scanning-tunnelling-lithography atomic placement
entries.note: Precision at the cost of throughput.

entries.name: Topological / III-V hybrid material stacks
entries.note: Materials science is the critical path for topological approaches.

entries.name: Silicon spin-qubit device fabrication
suppliers: Photonic Inc., Quantum Motion, Diraq (each in-house flows)
entries.note: Shared device substrate between monolithic and optically-linked spin architectures.
